name: Human effort per task
what: The hours of people time a task needs from preparation through review, correction and rework. A workflow is only a win if this number falls and stays down.
stage: Any task repeated weekly or more often, where the manual baseline can be measured before the build starts.
lever: Map the task, time the manual baseline, remove steps first, and only then add automation to what is left.
whereUsed: A 30% cut in manual outreach at CampK12 across a 400+ person workforce, and an estimated 20-30 founder hours back every month from nine pipelines for a Toronto founder.

name: Output accuracy
what: The share of outputs that are correct and usable on real inputs without a person fixing them. Speed means nothing if quality slips.
stage: Before a workflow touches customers, money or data that people rely on.
lever: Test with real inputs and edge cases, add validation checks, and keep human review before any consequential action.
whereUsed: Python automation frameworks at Accenture for banking and healthcare clients cut post-deployment defects by 15%.

name: Turnaround time
what: The elapsed time from request to finished output, measured separately from effort. A fast workflow with a long queue is still slow.
stage: When people wait on the result, such as outreach, reporting, screening or onboarding.
lever: Run steps in parallel and remove handoffs that only pass work along.
whereUsed: Nine parallel B2B pipelines produced 2,314 contacts and $1.47M CAD of prospect pipeline in 90 days.

name: Adoption without help
what: The share of the intended users who run the workflow on their own without asking its builder for help. A workflow that depends on its creator is a liability.
stage: At handoff, and again after the first month of real use.
lever: Write a one page operating guide, train the team on their own tasks, and make the next step obvious at every point.
whereUsed: Every workflow I ship follows this. The SOP Generator on the Shipped page exists to produce those guides quickly.

name: Cost per run
what: Model and tool spend per completed task, compared with the human effort it replaces.
stage: When volume grows and small per run costs start to add up.
lever: Use the smallest model that holds quality, cache repeated steps, and trim the input before it is sent.
whereUsed: The tools on the Shipped page cap input size and strip contact details before any text reaches a model.
